findings: Risk statement correctly identifies that evidence or attestation could be misinterpreted as truth or proof of correct outcome.
Required control mandates limitations, forbidden-claim tests, and review of every public wording surface.
Stop condition TRUTH_OR_CORRECTNESS_INFERENCE_PRESENT is well-defined and detectable.
Control is procedural and depends on consistent execution across all surfaces; residual risk remains if any surface is missed.
required_corrections: Define a concrete enumeration or discovery mechanism for all public wording surfaces to ensure review coverage is complete.
Specify the exact forbidden-claim test criteria and pass/fail thresholds.
residual_risks: Undiscovered or newly created public wording surfaces may escape review.
Forbidden-claim tests may not cover novel phrasings that imply truth or correctness.

findings: Risk statement correctly identifies that a verification result could be misconstrued as permission or operational authorization.
Required control demands non-elevation language, a separate decision reference, and a negative case.
Stop condition VERIFICATION_TO_PERMISSION_INFERENCE_PRESENT is well-defined.
Control relies on language discipline and structural separation; residual risk exists if downstream consumers ignore the separation.
required_corrections: Define the exact format and placement of the separate decision reference.
Specify the negative case template and ensure it is always co-published with verification results.
residual_risks: Downstream systems or human readers may still infer permission from verification despite non-elevation language.
Negative case may be overlooked if not prominently displayed.

findings: Risk statement correctly identifies that an attestation could be marketed as a certificate or certified Agent.
Required control imposes a ban on certificate claims until an independent authorized certification system exists.
Stop condition CERTIFICATE_OR_CERTIFIED_AGENT_CLAIM_PRESENT is clear and binary.
Ban is absolute and does not depend on procedural execution, reducing residual risk.
required_corrections: Define the criteria for recognizing an independent authorized certification system to know when the ban may be lifted.
residual_risks: Third parties outside VEAP governance may still make certificate claims referencing VEAP attestations.

findings: Risk statement correctly identifies that schema validity or conformance results could be presented as production proof.
Required control mandates publication of exact maturity, scope, executed count, limitations, and a production-claim prohibition.
Stop condition PRODUCTION_PROOF_INFERENCE_PRESENT is well-defined.
Control is disclosure-based; residual risk remains if readers ignore or misunderstand published limitations.
required_corrections: Specify the exact format and location for publishing maturity, scope, executed count, and limitations.
Define enforcement mechanism for the production-claim prohibition.
residual_risks: Published limitations may be ignored or misunderstood by downstream consumers.
Production-claim prohibition may be violated without detection.

findings: Risk statement correctly identifies that partial or sampled observations could be presented as complete execution history.
Required control mandates propagation of completeness, sampling, drop, partial, and unknown status without silent fill.
Stop condition COMPLETENESS_STATUS_MISSING_OR_ELEVATED is well-defined.
Control depends on consistent status propagation across all data paths; residual risk exists if any path silently fills or drops status.
required_corrections: Define the exact status vocabulary and encoding for completeness, sampling, drop, partial, and unknown.
Specify audit or monitoring mechanism to detect silent fill or status elevation.
residual_risks: Silent fill or status elevation may occur in undocumented data paths.
Status metadata may be stripped or ignored by downstream systems.

findings: Risk statement correctly identifies that VEAP could become a second canonical owner for DBOS, EEOAP, or verifier objects.
Required control enforces the ownership crosswalk, opaque references, and conflict fail-closed semantics.
Stop condition SECOND_CANONICAL_OWNER_CLAIM_PRESENT is clear and binary.
Fail-closed semantics ensure that any ownership conflict blocks rather than silently proceeding.
required_corrections: Document the exact ownership crosswalk mapping and ensure it is versioned and auditable.
residual_risks: Crosswalk mapping errors could cause false conflicts or missed conflicts.
Opaque references may complicate debugging if not accompanied by adequate logging.

findings: Risk statement correctly identifies that a SAEE evaluation or recommendation could be converted into decision or execution.
Required control mandates advisory labels, separate decision and authorization, and prohibition of writeback.
Stop condition EVALUATION_TO_DECISION_OR_EXECUTION_INFERENCE_PRESENT is well-defined.
Control depends on labeling discipline and architectural separation; residual risk exists if downstream systems bypass the separation.
required_corrections: Define the exact advisory label format and ensure it is machine-readable.
Specify the architectural boundary that enforces the writeback prohibition.
residual_risks: Downstream systems may ignore advisory labels and treat evaluations as decisions.
Writeback prohibition may be circumvented through indirect channels.

Evidence cited is limited to the supplied source document and does not establish truth.
Evaluation does not confer authority; recommendation does not constitute a decision; decision does not constitute execution; capability does not constitute permission.
All false effects are preserved: no authority, ownership, crosswalk acceptance, risk acceptance, implementation, commercial offer, certification, release, or deployment is approved.
